note: Bermuda, read on the Department of Immigration's own pages on gov.bm on 2026-10-30. Anyone working in Bermuda who isn't Bermudian, a spouse of one or a Permanent Resident's Certificate holder needs a work permit, applied for by the employer (read as work for the sponsor, and as applied for from either side of the border, since the pages name no place). A performer engaged for a single period of 14 days or less in professional sport or entertainment takes the short-term permit at $400 a person (up to five; $200 for each beyond the fifth in a group). A Standard Work Permit lets an employer hire a foreign national once it shows no Bermudian, spouse, belonger or PRC holder was suitably qualified or available; one year costs $1,015 (two $2,530, up to five $6,510); short-term permits up to six months cost $705 to $1,070. A Permanent Resident's Certificate costs $50,000 under section 31A and $3,310 under section 31B of the Bermuda Immigration and Protection Act 1956; who qualifies under each isn't on the pages read, so neither fee nor any years to it are kept. Naturalisation as a British Overseas Territories citizen costs $1,050; the years it asks aren't read, so no route is said to count.

sources.said: Bermudian, or be a Permanent Resident’s Certificate (PRC) holder. If you are not you must have a valid work permit. ... The purpose of a Standard Work Permit is to allow all organizations in Bermuda to employ foreign nationals if they can demonstrate that a Bermudian, Spouse of a Bermudian, Belonger, Spouse of a Belonger, or PRC holder was not suitably qualified or available to be hired.
